minutes.headline: Select Board voted to put five marijuana-use prohibition questions on the town ballot at the Planning Board's request.
minutes.summary: The meeting was dominated by a joint session with the Planning Board on placing five marijuana-use questions on the ballot, with heated public comment and board disagreement. what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to put five marijuana prohibition questions on the town ballot, as the Planning Board requested, in a joint session.
Public comment on the marijuana articles ran both ways: some urged waiting for public input and impact information, others wanted the question put to voters.
The board approved an earth removal permit and held the closure permit until the Planning Board approves it.
The board passed on the Chapter 61B right of first refusal for the Northfield Road property, letting it lapse with no action.
The board will ask town counsel again about the Northfield Road lapse and may take it up on January 22.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked to vote on whether to prohibit marijuana uses in town, so the ballot wording and the impacts shared beforehand will shape that choice.
Letting the Northfield Road right of first refusal lapse means the town is not exercising its option to buy that land, which bears on open space and on how Chapter 61 conversion revenue is used.
